# Instance chart {#sec-instance-charts} ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"} ## Theme: `theme_gushers()` Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_gushers()`, built from Fruit Gushers: a white plate background, a red frame and title, red, green, teal, orange, and pink fruit snack marks, and a Chalkboard title. ::: :::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}
::: {.cell layout-align="right"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](instance_chart_files/figure-html/full_code_display-1.png){fig-align='right' width=60% height=60%} ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"} **Requirements:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a categorical variable** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric (count) variable** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric (date) variable** ::: :::: ## Description An instance chart shows each time a group comes up as time goes on.[^instances] Time goes on the `x` axis, and each group gets its own place on the `y` axis.[^categorical] Each time a group comes up, we most often show it with a short mark that stands straight up, using `geom_point()` with `shape` `124` (the `"|"` mark).[^ticks] Color and how much we can see through each mark[^saturation] also show the groups and how many times each one comes up. ## Set up ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **PACKAGES:** ::: Bring in the code we'll use.[^packages] ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # for data manipulation library(tidyr) # for expand_grid() ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DATA:** ::: Fruit Gushers are small, soft fruit snacks with juice inside, in many flavors, and they came out in 1991. To sell them, they showed a kid whose head turned into a big piece of fruit.[^ads] Fruit snacks were already the money[^currency] at the lunch table, where kids ate in the middle of the school day, and a new Gushers flavor made its fruit worth more. We'll make up[^simulate] how many times each flavor changed hands at one lunch table each year from 1980 to 2005.[^trades] Each flavor in `snack_flavors` has a mean number of trades each year `before` the year Gushers made it (`debut`, a year we made up) and a mean `after` it (berry punch comes in 1992, sour apple in 1998, and mystery in 2001).[^average] A count is how many times something happens. `rpois()` picks each year's count (`n`) using the mean that goes with that year.[^rpois] Starting with `set.seed()`[^seed] means you'll get the same 208 flavor years every time you run the code below. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} snack_flavors <- tibble( flavor = c("Strawberry", "Lime", "Blue raspberry", "Orange", # eight Gushers flavors "Watermelon", "Berry punch", "Sour apple", "Mystery"), before = c(4, 0.3, 1, 1.5, 0.2, 1, 0.05, 0.05), # average yearly trades before the debut after = c(8, 1.5, 4, 1.5, 0.8, 1.5, 2, 3), # average yearly trades after the debut debut = c(1991, 1991, 1991, 1991, 1991, 1992, 1998, 2001) # pretend debut year for each flavor ) set.seed(1993) # same trades every time the code runs lunch_trades <- expand_grid(year = 1980:2005, snack_flavors) |> # every flavor in every year mutate( flavor = factor(flavor, levels = snack_flavors$flavor), # keep the order above avg_n = if_else(year < debut, before, after), # pick the average for that year n = rpois(n(), lambda = avg_n) # number of trades that year ) |> select(year, flavor, debut, avg_n, n) glimpse(lunch_trades) #> Rows: 208 #> Columns: 5 #> $ year 1980, 1980, 1980, 1980, 1980, 198… #> $ flavor Strawberry, Lime, Blue raspberry,… #> $ debut 1991, 1991, 1991, 1991, 1991, 199… #> $ avg_n 4.00, 0.30, 1.00, 1.50, 0.20, 1.0… #> $ n 3, 0, 0, 2, 0, 1, 0, 0, 6, 0, 1, … ``` ::: ::: An instance chart only shows the years a flavor changed hands, so we'll take out the years with no trades[^filter] and keep the rest in `gushers_trades`. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} gushers_trades <- lunch_trades |> filter(n > 0) # keep only the years with at least one trade glimpse(gushers_trades) #> Rows: 128 #> Columns: 5 #> $ year 1980, 1980, 1980, 1981, 1981, 198… #> $ flavor Strawberry, Orange, Berry punch, … #> $ debut 1991, 1991, 1992, 1991, 1991, 199… #> $ avg_n 4.0, 1.5, 1.0, 4.0, 1.0, 1.5, 1.0… #> $ n 3, 2, 1, 6, 1, 3, 3, 2, 1, 3, 1, … ``` ::: ::: ## Distribution An instance chart comes from two things: whether a flavor shows up in a year (the mark), and how many times it shows up (how much we can see through it).[^shading] The open spaces between the marks matter just as much as the marks, and the number of open spaces turns on how much kids want the flavor.[^popular] Below we'll move from the counts, to a graph, to the rule behind it.[^formula] ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **COUNT IT:** ::: Start with lime in the five years before and after Gushers came out. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} lunch_trades |> filter(flavor == "Lime", year >= 1986, year <= 1995) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Before 1991, most years have no lime trades at all. Below we count the years with no trades (`zero_years`) for each flavor, before and after the year it came out. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} zero_counts <- lunch_trades |> mutate(era = if_else(year < debut, "before", "after")) |> group_by(flavor, era) |> summarise(years = n(), zero_years = sum(n == 0), .groups = "drop") |> pivot_wider(names_from = era, values_from = c(years, zero_years)) |> select(flavor, years_before, zero_years_before, years_after, zero_years_after) zero_counts ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Lime went 8 of 11 years without a trade before Gushers, and only 3 of 15 years after it. Strawberry, the flavor kids wanted most, never had a year without a trade. ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DRAW IT:** ::: The graph below shows lime's count for each year as a bar (even the years with 0) and shows the same years as instance marks under the bars. Every open space in the marks is a year whose bar stops at 0. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} lime <- lunch_trades |> filter(flavor == "Lime") ggplot(lime, aes(x = year)) + geom_col(aes(y = n), fill = "#4E6B44") + geom_point(data = filter(lime, n > 0), aes(y = -0.5), shape = 124, size = 5, color = "#D01D27") + geom_vline(xintercept = 1990.5, linetype = "dashed") + annotate("text", x = 1990.3, y = max(lime$n), label = "Gushers come out", hjust = 1) + labs(title = "Lime trades each year", x = "Year", y = "Lime trades") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](instance_chart_files/figure-html/draw_inst-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **NAME IT:** ::: Each year's count comes from a [rule for counts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisson_distribution)[^poisson] that uses the mean for that flavor, before or after the year it came out: $$ n_{\text{flavor, year}} \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda), \quad P(n = 0) = e^{-\lambda} $$ The chance of a year with no trades turns only on $\lambda$, the mean. Before Gushers, lime's mean is 0.3 trades a year, so $P(n = 0) = e^{-0.3} \approx 0.74$, and we'd look for about $11 \times 0.74 \approx 8.1$ years with no trades out of 11.[^expect] After Gushers, the mean goes up to 1.5, so $P(n = 0) = e^{-1.5} \approx 0.22$ and we'd look for about 3.3 years with no trades out of 15. Strawberry's mean is 8 trades a year after Gushers, so a year with no trades has a chance of $e^{-8} \approx 0.0003$ (almost never). That's why flavors that kids don't often trade look like marks with spaces between them, and flavors they trade a lot look like lines with no breaks. Try changing lime's `after` number to `5`, and lime gets a mark in almost every year from 1991 on. ## Grammar ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **CODE:** ::: - Make the words around the graph[^labels] with `labs()` - Start the graph with `ggplot()` and give it `data` - Put `year` on the `x` axis and `flavor` on the `y` axis, and give each `flavor` its own `color`[^map] - Add `geom_point()`, let `n` set how much we can see through each mark (`alpha`),[^alpha] and set the `shape` to `124` and `size` to `5` - Most years have only a few trades, so we make the lightest marks stronger with `scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.35, 1))` (if we don't, the lightest marks are hard to see) - Take away the `color` key[^legend] with `guides()` (the flavors are already on the `y` axis) ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} labs_inst_gushers <- labs( title = "Fruit Gushers", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "Fruit snack trades at one lunch table, 1980 - 2005", x = "Year", y = "Flavor", alpha = "Trades per year") ggp2_inst_gushers <- ggplot(data = gushers_trades, mapping = aes(x = year, y = flavor, color = flavor)) + geom_point(aes(alpha = n), shape = 124, size = 5) + scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.35, 1)) + guides(color = "none") ggp2_inst_gushers + labs_inst_gushers ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **GRAPH:** ::: ::: {.cell layout-nrow="1"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](instance_chart_files/figure-html/create_graph_inst-1.png){width=100% height=100%} ::: ::: ## More info ### Color with `cut_interval()` `ggplot2` has three ways of cutting a column of numbers into groups: `cut_interval()`, `cut_number()`, and `cut_width()`.[^cut] We'll use `cut_interval()` to make an `n_range` column, which cuts the counts for each year (`n`) into groups that are each as wide as `length`.[^length] ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} gushers_trades_range <- gushers_trades |> mutate( n_range = ggplot2::cut_interval(x = n, length = 3) # group trade counts into bins 3 wide ) gushers_trades_range |> count(n_range) # rows in each bin ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Below we can see that each group of counts is written [with its lowest and highest numbers](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/cut_interval.html):[^interval] `"(a,b]"` - Most of the marks fall in the lowest group, and every count over 9 comes from strawberry after Gushers came out. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} labs_inst_gushers_range <- labs( title = "Fruit Gushers", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "Fruit snack trades at one lunch table, 1980 - 2005", x = "Year", y = "Flavor", color = "Trades per year") ggp2_inst_gushers_range <- ggplot(data = gushers_trades_range, mapping = aes(x = year, y = flavor, color = n_range)) + geom_point(aes(alpha = n), shape = 124, size = 4) + scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.35, 1)) + guides(alpha = "none") # the color key already shows the trade counts ggp2_inst_gushers_range + labs_inst_gushers_range ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](instance_chart_files/figure-html/code_graph_inst_range-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: ### Facets with `cut_number()` To show small graphs,[^facets] we'll make two more columns: `year_range` and `group`: - `year_range` uses `ggplot2::cut_number()` to cut `year` into three groups with about the same number of marks in each, then we make a name for each group from its first and last year - `group` is a column with two set values:[^factor] `"Single fruit"` and `"Berry blends"` (blue raspberry and berry punch) ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} gushers_trades_fct <- gushers_trades |> mutate( year_grp = ggplot2::cut_number(year, n = 3, labels = FALSE) # three groups of years with similar counts ) |> group_by(year_grp) |> mutate(year_range = paste(min(year), "-", max(year))) |> # label each group with its years ungroup() |> mutate( year_range = factor(year_range, levels = unique(year_range[order(year)])), # earliest to latest group = if_else(flavor %in% c("Blue raspberry", "Berry punch"), "Berry blends", "Single fruit"), # two flavor groups group = factor(group, levels = c("Single fruit", "Berry blends")) ) ``` ::: ::: Below we can see how many flavor years with at least one trade fall in each `year_range` and `group`[^crosstab] ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} gushers_trades_fct |> count(year_range, group) |> pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = n) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: In the graph, the words over each small graph show its years, so the words at the top[^subtitle] show the first and last year of all the trades. - We can also change the `shape` in `geom_point()` to the straight up mark (`"|"`)[^pipe] - `facet_grid()` puts the flavor groups in rows and the year groups in columns. With `scales = "free"`, each row keeps only its own flavors, so the flavors line up across the row, and each column picks its own numbers along the `x` axis,[^breaks] so we set them every five years with `scale_x_continuous()` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} labs_inst_gushers_facet <- labs( title = "Fruit Gushers", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "Fruit snack trades at one lunch table, 1980 - 2005", x = "Year", y = "Flavor") ggp2_inst_gushers_facet <- ggplot(gushers_trades_fct, mapping = aes(x = year, y = flavor)) + geom_point(aes(alpha = n, color = flavor), shape = "|", size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2005, by = 5)) + scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.35, 1)) + facet_grid(group ~ year_range, scales = "free") ggp2_inst_gushers_facet + labs_inst_gushers_facet ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](instance_chart_files/figure-html/code_graph_inst_facet-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: [^instances]: An instance chart (or instance graph) displays frequencies (or "instances") of different categorical values over time. [^categorical]: Each separate categorical item. [^ticks]: Vertical hashes; shape `124` is the pipe character `"|"`. [^saturation]: Transparency (`alpha`). [^packages]: Install packages. [^ads]: Commercials. [^currency]: Currency. [^simulate]: Simulate. [^trades]: How many packs of each flavor were traded. [^average]: The average number of trades per year before and after each flavor's pretend Gushers `debut`. [^rpois]: `rpois()` draws each year's count from a Poisson distribution with the matching average (`lambda = avg_n`). [^seed]: Setting the seed. [^filter]: Filter out. [^shading]: Transparency (`alpha`). [^popular]: How popular the flavor is. [^formula]: The formula. [^poisson]: A Poisson distribution, with the average for that flavor and era. [^expect]: The expected number of empty years. [^labels]: Create labels. [^map]: Map `year` to `x`, `flavor` to `y`, and `color` to `flavor`. [^alpha]: Map `n` to `alpha` (transparency). [^legend]: Legend. [^cut]: Functions for splitting numerical variables into equal width intervals, groups with equal counts, or bins of a set width. [^length]: The `length` argument sets the width of each interval. [^interval]: Interval notation: `(` leaves `a` out of the interval and `]` keeps `b` in it. [^facets]: Facets. [^factor]: A factor variable with two levels. [^crosstab]: A cross table of `year_range` and `group`; each cell counts rows (flavor years with at least one trade), not trades. [^subtitle]: Labels (here, the subtitle). [^pipe]: The pipe operator. [^breaks]: Breaks.
